title: Persuasion Mission
description: Integrate the Unit language to complete a sustained C1 mission about persuasion & rhetoric.
objectives: Integrate the Unit language to complete a sustained C1 mission about persuasion & rhetoric.

stages.title: Understand meaning and form
stages.instructions: Read the concept, pattern, examples, contrast, common issue, and recap.

blocks.text: The communicative aim of this lesson is to integrate the Unit language to complete a sustained C1 mission about persuasion & rhetoric. The central language focus is integrated persuasion review. In the context of persuasion & rhetoric, form and meaning work together: first identify the relationship between the ideas, then choose wording that makes that relationship clear to another person. At C1, precision includes stance, register, and information structure. Make the relationship between claims explicit, qualify what cannot be fully supported, and adapt the wording to the audience without losing nuance.

blocks.english: This example illustrates anticipate an objection clearly.
blocks.explanation: This model establishes the main communicative move.

blocks.english: We should consider audience concern carefully.
blocks.explanation: This model develops or qualifies the message.

blocks.text: Start with the model “This example illustrates anticipate an objection clearly.” It establishes a useful direction for the exchange. The second model, “We should consider audience concern carefully.” adds another layer: a reason, implication, contrast, or response. Notice how each complete chunk does a communicative job. Practice replacing one detail while preserving the original grammar, stance, and register. Then connect the revised sentence to a relevant consequence or example instead of changing topic abruptly.

A useful pattern for this lesson is: integrated persuasion review. Use it when the situation genuinely calls for that meaning. Contrast matters: a direct factual statement presents information, while a qualified or hypothetical form changes the speaker's commitment to it. The choice should be driven by evidence, time reference, relationship, and purpose. In listening, pay attention not only to individual words but also to linkers, stress, and the speaker's degree of certainty.

blocks.title: Contrast
blocks.text: Compare a direct statement with language shaped by integrated persuasion review; the intended meaning determines the form.

A common issue is to select an advanced-looking form without maintaining its meaning across the sentence. That can create a mismatch in time, stance, or register. Check three things: what happened or is being proposed, how certain the speaker is, and what response is expected. For persuasion mission, clarity comes from a coherent message rather than maximum complexity. The later stages recycle the same vocabulary and expressions so that recognition becomes controlled production and then flexible interaction. This sixth Lesson consolidates Lessons 1–5 and introduces no major new grammar. Select among the Unit patterns according to the communicative need.

blocks.title: Common issue
blocks.text: Do not add complexity that changes the time reference, degree of certainty, or relationship with the listener.

stages.title: Listen for meaning and stance
stages.instructions: Listen first, then reveal the text and notice connections, register, and emphasis.

segments.text: To begin with, This example illustrates anticipate an objection clearly. We should consider audience concern carefully.
In this situation, We should consider audience concern carefully. The discussion highlighted call to action.
From another perspective, The discussion highlighted call to action. A clear explanation addresses measured tone directly.
More specifically, A clear explanation addresses measured tone directly. The speaker emphasized persuasive impact.
Even so, The speaker emphasized persuasive impact. Our response should account for compelling reason.
As a result, Our response should account for compelling reason. This example illustrates appeal to values clearly.
On reflection, This example illustrates appeal to values clearly. We should consider credible evidence carefully.
